name: Balanced power plan
summary: The Windows default. Speed follows what you are doing.
what: Makes the Balanced plan the active power plan.
benefit: Good performance when you need it and lower power use when idle.
advice: Suggested for most laptops and everyday desktops. Pick it to go back after trying another plan.
facts: Windows ships it as the default plan
Scales processor speed up and down automatically
Only one power plan is active at a time

name: High performance power plan
what: Makes the High performance plan the active power plan.
benefit: Keeps the processor more ready, which can help games and heavy work feel steadier.
risk: Low. Uses more power, runs warmer and drains a laptop battery faster.
advice: Suggested for desktops that stay plugged in. Skip it on laptops that run on battery.
facts: Uses more power and can run hotter
A laptop on battery will drain faster
Only one power plan is active at a time

name: Ultimate Performance power plan
summary: A workstation plan that cuts small power saving delays.
what: Creates the Ultimate Performance plan from the built in template if it is missing, then makes it active.
benefit: Removes tiny wake and sleep delays in the processor, which can help latency sensitive work on a plugged in desktop.
risk: Low. The highest power use of any plan. Some laptops do not offer it.
advice: Suggested for plugged in desktops and workstations. Skip it on laptops and for everyday use.
facts: Made from a built in template and named Ultimate Performance
Aimed at workstations and high end PCs
Not meant for running on battery
Reverting switches back to the plan you had before

name: Power saver plan
what: Makes the Power saver plan the active power plan.
benefit: Longer battery life and lower heat.
risk: Low. The PC can feel slower under load.
advice: Suggested when battery life matters more than speed.
facts: Lowers processor speed to save energy
Only one power plan is active at a time

name: Turn off hibernation
summary: Free disk space by removing the hibernation file.
what: Turns hibernation off, which deletes the hibernation file on the system drive.
benefit: Frees the disk space the hibernation file used. By default Windows sizes it as a share of your memory.
risk: Low. Hibernate is no longer offered. Fast Startup also turns off because it relies on hibernation.
advice: Suggested for desktops that never hibernate, or when disk space is tight. Skip it on laptops that hibernate to save battery.
facts: Fast Startup depends on hibernation, so it stops too
